text.title: Competitive Intelligence Core Rules
text.summary: Testable rules grounding the Competitive Intelligence methodology. Every rule pairs a binary check with sourced rationale, plus the universal skip-this-methodology gate. Folds in the former monitoring-framework file: Signal sources, monitoring frequencies, platform landscape, and CI evolution from reactive to predictive. Operational best practices from the former tools file are rules here; the tool list is in `content/04-procedure.xml`.

rule.statement: Monitor each signal category at its natural change rate: pricing and funding weekly, feature launches and website changes daily, hiring and content/SEO monthly.
rule.rationale: Polling too slowly misses time-sensitive funding and pricing signals. Polling too frequently on slow-moving signals wastes quota and generates noise. Source-by-source cadence is in the Signal sources section below.

rule.statement: Stamp every battlecard with a generation date and enforce a 14-day TTL; a 2-week-old battlecard with confident tone is worse than no battlecard. Older battlecards MUST NOT be distributed.
rule.rationale: Sales reps trust dated artifacts. Stale-but-confident claims actively damage deals.

rule.statement: Assign Haiku to mechanical collection and classification; Sonnet to synthesis and battlecard writing; Opus to threat assessment and scenario planning — never invert this. Separate "what changed" (Haiku, mechanical) from "so what" (Opus, judgment). Mixing them costs 10x and adds hallucination.
rule.rationale: Mixing reasoning-grade models into collection tasks adds 10x cost with no marginal accuracy gain. Mixing fast models into threat analysis produces hallucinated strategic claims. Opus reasoning on raw HTML diffs is wasteful and noisy. Haiku distills the signal; Opus interprets the pattern.

rule.statement: Every digest and battlecard must pass a fact-checker agent that HEAD-requests every cited URL before the document is distributed.
rule.rationale: LLMs invent URLs like /pricing/enterprise that never existed. Publishing an invented citation to a sales rep destroys trust in the entire CI function.

rule.statement: Every factual claim MUST reference an event_id from the collector NDJSON.
rule.rationale: Unsourced claims are liabilities; provenance is the audit trail.

rule.statement: Emit one event per delta, never aggregate inside the collector — keeps the audit trail clean and lets the synthesizer see the raw timeline.
rule.rationale: Aggregated events hide the sequence of competitor moves. The synthesizer needs the timeline to detect acceleration patterns.

rule.statement: Subscribe to competitor changelog/RSS first; scraping is the fallback. APIs > RSS > scrape > screenshot diff.
rule.rationale: APIs are reliable and ToS-compliant. Scraping is fragile and legally ambiguous. Use the most reliable source available per competitor.

rule.statement: Pick a platform tier matched to your scale: Crayon/Klue for mid-market automation and battlecard distribution; Contify Athena for agentic unstructured-content analysis; AlphaSense for filings and expert-call transcripts.

rationale.source: Crayon / Klue / Contify / AlphaSense product documentation (2025)

rule.rationale: Over-engineering CI infrastructure before you have 3+ named competitors and an action loop wastes budget. Under-investing means alerts are never acted on. The platform landscape is listed in the CI platform comparison section below.

rule.statement: Build toward predictive CI by feeding historical event logs into a threat-scoring model calibrated quarterly against actual lost deals. Calibrate threat scores against actual lost deals quarterly; recalibrate the prompt if the score does not predict losses.
rule.rationale: Descriptive CI is table stakes. Predictive CI compresses the gap between a competitor signal and your strategic response from weeks to hours. An uncalibrated threat score becomes a noise source. Quarterly calibration ties CI to revenue impact.

rule.statement: Track yourself with the same pipeline to catch what your own marketing site exposes to competitors.
rule.rationale: CI is bidirectional. What you publish about pricing, hiring, and product reveals your strategy to the same tools your competitors use.

rule.statement: Apply this methodology only if all entries in `## Applies If` hold and none of `## Skip If` triggers; otherwise abort and route to the correct methodology.

rationale.source: F-066 spec — decision tree minimum form

rule.rationale: A misrouted methodology produces wrong-shape output; the explicit skip rule is the universal default branch from the decision tree.

section.title: Background
section.p: Current (2025): Reactive and descriptive — tells you what competitors did after they did it. Emerging (2026): Predictive and prescriptive — anticipates competitor moves and recommends strategic responses via multi-agent pipelines.

list.item: Pricing changes: Crayon, Klue + manual — weekly
Feature launches: Product Hunt, Twitter — daily
Crayon: CI automation, battlecard generation, partial REST API
Klue: Market intelligence distribution to Salesforce/Slack, partial REST API
Contify Athena (2025): Agentic AI engine for unstructured-content reasoning
AlphaSense: Multi-source intel (filings, transcripts, expert calls), API + summaries
Kompyte (Semrush): Real-time site/SEO delta tracking at scale, webhook + API
Valona Intelligence: Multilingual CI for EU/APAC competitors, limited API
Weekly digest: product team — Delta events per competitor, scored by signal type
Monthly threat assessment: leadership — Evidence-based threat score 1-5, recommended action
Quarterly feature comparison: sales, marketing — Full feature matrix vs competitors
Quarterly strategic report: executive — Scenario planning, market shifts
Real-time battlecards: sales reps — Auto-regenerated on high-severity events, TTL 14 days
